title: Wild Rice, Red Pepper and Shallot Pancakes with Smoked Salmon
changes_from_base: A savoury milk batter lightened with whisked egg whites and filled with cooked wild rice, charred red pepper and soft shallots, served with smoked salmon and chive soured cream; stirring the pepper and shallots into the batter with the rice is my own adjustment, as the source cooks them but does not say when they go in.
summary: Fluffy wild rice pancakes flecked with sweet roasted red pepper and shallot, paired with smoked salmon and a chive-flecked soured cream.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
chopped chives, plus more to garnish
fine sea salt or table salt, and black pepper

steps.title: Char
steps.text: Char the 1 red pepper under a hot grill, then remove the skin, stem and seeds and chop finely.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Heat the 1 tbsp olive oil and 14 g butter in a small frying pan and cook the pepper with the 2 shallots until soft.

steps.title: Cream
steps.text: Mix the 180 ml soured cream with the 2 tbsp chives, salt and pepper and set aside.

steps.title: Batter
steps.text: Sift the 125 g flour and 1 tbsp baking powder into a bowl, add the 1 tsp salt and 240 ml milk and mix well, then beat in the 3 egg yolks one at a time and stir in the 165 g wild rice and the pepper and shallot mixture.

steps.title: Fold
steps.text: Whisk the 3 egg whites to stiff peaks and fold into the batter.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Heat a griddle until a drop of water sizzles, grease with olive oil, then drop 30 ml batter per pancake to make 8 cm rounds and brown on both sides.

steps.title: Keep
steps.text: Keep the pancakes warm in a low oven.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve 2 pancakes per person with the smoked salmon, a spoonful of chive cream and a scattering of chives.

tips: Pat the charred red pepper and the cooked wild rice dry before stirring them into the batter, so the pancakes stay light rather than soggy.
Fold in the whisked egg whites gently to keep the pancakes light and fluffy.
Make sure the griddle is properly hot before the first batch for an even golden colour.
Keep finished pancakes warm in a low oven while you cook the rest.
storage: Keep the cooked pancakes warm in a low oven until ready to serve. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
